notes: Toy configuration for VS3 Task 9 planted fixture BR-TRAP-1 (.kiro spec ascension-trials-scalable-two-player-analysis): an illegal-entry trap where the tempting, high-reward Trial cannot be entered legally by the acting side and the best-response oracle must avoid it (REQ-7.3 'a tempting-but-illegal allocation the oracle must avoid').

Two energy domains (void, flux). Trial 'grand' (reward first=10) requires TWO energy sources (source_count class:energy minimum 2); Trial 'minor' (reward first=4) is mono (source_count class:energy minimum 1 maximum 1). Optional allocation with residue, winner-take-all with shared-full ties, local total_power tiebreak, no final tiebreak.

Acting side holds power in ONE energy domain only (void), so any entry on 'grand' has a single source (< 2) and is illegal: the resolver drops it and awards it 0 (ignore_entry). The 10-point 'grand' reward is therefore unreachable no matter how much void is piled on it. The only legal Recognition Points come from the 4-point mono Trial 'minor'. A greedy oracle chasing the 10 would place void on 'grand' and score 0; the correct best response places void on 'minor' and banks 4. Oracle transcribed from the rules (eligibility source-count predicate, model v2.1 §4.1; illegal-entry drop, spec v1.1 §7.3), not reverse-engineered from engine output (REQ-9.4).
